source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Bar Basics: Signal Bars, Entry Bars, Setups, and Candle Patterns

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode. Helpers: range(n) = high[n]-low[n]; body(n) = close[n]-open[n]; avgRange(N) = average of range over the N bars ending at bar 1; tick = instrument minimum price move (structural constant).

candidates.name: GenericSignalBarBreakoutEntry
candidates.quote: that means that every bar is a signal bar for both long and short trades, with both bulls and bears entering on the breakout of both the top and the bottom.
candidates.description: Primitive: base stop-entry mechanism. Every bar is a potential signal bar; a close beyond its high (long) / low (short) is the breakout entry, mechanized as close-then-next-open.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the prior (signal) bar's high; sell stop one tick below its low
notes: Base primitive other chapter-4 candidates build on; identical to the existing corpus rule at lookback=1.

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutFade
candidates.quote: There will also be bears who will short on a limit order at the high of the prior bar, expecting the breakout to fail. They hope that the market will trade below the low of their entry bar on the bar after they short.
candidates.description: Long side (book's example is the mirror, a short): the bar two back made a fresh low relative to the bar before it, but this bar closes back above that low, confirming the breakdown failed. Buy above this bar's high at the next open.
candidates.book_order_type: book's short case: sell limit at the high of the prior bar anticipating failure, stop above the entry bar if wrong; mechanized here as a confirmed-failure stop entry, which gives up the earlier limit fill
notes: Generic version of the outside-bar-specific failed-breakout fade mined elsewhere (e.g., T07-17); no outside-bar requirement here.

candidates.name: StrongTrendBar
candidates.quote: Strong bull trend bar in a bull spike.
candidates.description: Primitive: bar 0 is a 'strong' trend bar -- closes up (bull side) with a body that is most of its range AND a range at or above the recent average (not just any trend bar).

complexity.reason: average range over a window plus single-bar arithmetic

notes: Brooks gives no numbers for 'strong'; values are a reading of the qualifier.

candidates.name: SpikeContext
candidates.quote: Continuation signal in the spike phase of a strong trend: A continuation signal can be buying at the top of a bull trend or selling at the bottom of a bear trend.
candidates.description: Context filter primitive: the market is in the spike phase of a strong trend, approximated as at least K of the last N bars closing as trend bars in the same direction with no pause bar breaking the streak.
candidates.pseudocode: count over k in 1..N of (close[k] > open[k]) >= K

candidates.name: SpikeContinuationEntry
candidates.quote: Strong bull trend bar in a bull spike.
candidates.description: During the spike phase of a bull trend, this bar is itself a strong bull trend bar: buy above it as a with-trend continuation signal.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the strong trend bar's high

complexity.reason: inherits the window-count context plus a single-bar test

candidates.name: ReversalBar
candidates.description: Primitive: bar 0 is a bull reversal bar -- closes up, in the upper part of its range, with a lower tail. Working definition used before chapter 5 formalizes it.
notes: Chapter 5 gives the fuller, formal definition this is a placeholder for.

candidates.name: ReversalBarFailureContinuation
candidates.quote: Failed reversal attempt, including a reversal bar failure.
candidates.description: Long side: bar 1 was a would-be short signal (a bear reversal bar) but this bar closes below bar 1's low instead of triggering the short -- the failed reversal favors resumption of the up move; buy above this bar's high.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (close-based mechanization of a failed stop order)

candidates.name: FailedContinuationLow1Fade
candidates.quote: Failed continuation attempt, like buying below a low 1 signal bar in a bear trend that appears to be bottoming or shorting above a high 1 signal bar in a bull trend that appears to be topping.
candidates.description: A 'low 1' first-pullback signal bar in a bear trend that looks like it may be bottoming is broken to the downside as normal, but the breakout fails: fade it long. 'Low 1' pullback counting is not formalized in this chapter.

complexity.reason: depends on a High1/Low1 pullback-counting primitive not defined in this chapter; a design decision is needed before this is codeable

notes: Placeholder pending the H1/L1 counting primitive mined from the pullback-counting chapters.

candidates.name: ShavedBar
candidates.quote: Shaved bar: a bar with no tail at either the top or the bottom.
candidates.description: Primitive: bar 0 has (near) zero tail on both ends -- open/close sit at or very near both the high and the low.
notes: Used elsewhere as a 'strong signal bar' qualifier.

candidates.name: HigherLowBarInBullTrend
candidates.quote: Any bar that forms a higher low in a bull trend and a lower high in a bear trend.
candidates.description: In a bull trend, a bar whose low is above the prior bar's low is a buy setup (higher low).
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the higher-low bar's high

complexity.reason: two-bar comparison plus a trend-context read

notes: 'BullTrendContext' proxied by the corpus's Momentum rule (close above close N bars ago) pending a dedicated trend-context primitive.

candidates.name: ChannelBuyAtOrBelowPriorBar
candidates.quote: All bars in a channel: Buy at or below prior bar, sell at or above prior bar.
candidates.description: In an established channel, buy when this bar trades at or below the prior bar's low (approximating a limit entry within the channel).
candidates.book_order_type: buy limit at or below the prior bar's low

complexity.reason: 'channel' recognition needs pivot/line-projection design decisions covered in later chapters (15-16), not in this one

candidates.name: BeginnerTrendBarSignalFilter
candidates.quote: A beginning trader should enter only when the signal bar is also a trend bar in the direction of the trade, and should trade only in the direction of the trend.
candidates.description: Filter: require the signal bar (bar 1) to be a trend bar in the trade's direction and the market to be in a matching trend.

complexity.reason: single-bar test plus a trend-context read

candidates.name: CountertrendRequiresStrongerSignalBar
candidates.quote: In general, traders should require signal bars to be stronger for trend reversal entries than for trend pullback and trading range trades.
candidates.description: Graded filter: the required signal-bar 'strength' (body position, tail, size) rises the more countertrend the entry is; with-trend entries can use weak or even opposite-colored signal bars, but countertrend entries need a near-perfect one.

complexity.reason: a 'signal bar strength score' and the with-trend/countertrend classification both need design decisions before this can be coded

notes: Covers both directions of the heuristic: strict for reversals, lenient for with-trend pullbacks, per the same sentence.

candidates.name: OneTickTrapOffsetEntry
candidates.quote: For stocks, it is often better to place the entry stop at a couple of ticks beyond the potential signal bar because one-tick traps are common.
candidates.description: Require the close to clear the signal bar's high by an extra offset (in ticks) before entering, to avoid one-tick-trap fakeouts.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop a couple of ticks above the signal bar's high (stocks); one tick for futures per the base rule
notes: Offset is instrument-specific; Brooks gives 'a couple of ticks' for stocks vs. one tick generally.

candidates.name: SpikeEndBar
candidates.quote: every trend bar is a climax or part of a climax and the climax ends with the first pause bar... if there are three consecutive bull trend bars and then the next bar is a small bull trend bar with a prominent tail on the top, or an inside bar, a doji, or a bear trend bar, then the climax ended with the three bull trend bars.
candidates.description: Primitive/filter: a bull spike/climax is judged to have ended when, after a streak of K consecutive bull trend bars, this bar fails to also qualify as a (non-small, non-tailed) bull trend bar.
candidates.pseudocode: (count over k in 1..streakBars of (close[k] > open[k] && (close[k]-open[k]) >= bodyFraction*(high[k]-low[k])) == streakBars) && !(close[0] > open[0] && (close[0]-open[0]) >= bodyFraction*(high[0]-low[0]))

complexity.reason: streak detection ending exactly at a bar boundary is cross-bar state, not a plain window average

candidates.name: FollowThroughBar
candidates.quote: The bar after entry is the follow-through bar, and it is always better when there is a second bar in the direction of your entry.
candidates.description: Primitive: the bar immediately after entry that continues (does not reverse) in the trade's direction. No explicit numeric management action is tied to it in this chapter; recorded for later chapters that may use it to scale in or tighten stops.
notes: No concrete action attached in this chapter; kept for high recall in case a later chapter conditions management on it.

rejected.quote: It is usually best to enter on a stop at one tick above or below the prior bar and if the stop is not hit, to cancel the order and look for a new location for an order.
rejected.reason: pending-order lifecycle and discretionary re-placement ('a new location'), not a new bar-level condition beyond the base breakout entry

rejected.quote: Until you are consistently profitable and able to read quickly, it is best to not take the trade and to wait for a second entry instead. However, if you are confident that there are lots of trapped bears, then you can take the trade.
the vast majority of candle patterns are not helpful most of the time because they occur in price action where they have no high-probability predictive value.
rejected.reason: narrative skepticism about candle-pattern names; no threshold or condition stated

rejected.quote: Whenever a trader believes that there is an imbalance, he has an advantage, but it is always very small because there are always smart traders who believe the opposite.
rejected.reason: narrative about trader psychology/edge, no bar-level test

rejected.quote: Figure 4.1 ... Bar 4 was an entry bar off of an ii setup ... Bar 5 was an entry bar off of an inside bar breakout pullback.
rejected.reason: chart-example walkthrough; the ii/inside-bar/reversal-bar concepts it illustrates are already captured as primitives (T04-06) or belong to other chapters, no new mechanical statement

chapter_summary: Chapter 4 lays out signal-bar/entry-bar/follow-through terminology, the generic two-sided stop-entry mechanism, and a long enumerated list of common signal-bar/setup types (most of which are formally defined in other chapters). Its own mechanical content is the base breakout entry, a failed-breakout fade, a strong-trend-bar spike-continuation setup, a shaved-bar and reversal-bar primitive, a higher-low/channel setup, graded signal-bar-strength filters for beginners and for countertrend trades, a one-tick-trap offset parameter, and a climax/spike-end streak test. Several list items (ii/iii, ioi, oo, double top/bottom, trend-line-break pullbacks, high1/low1 patterns) are only named here and are fully defined in other chapters -- do not re-mine this chapter's enumeration as a novel source for those, just note it references them.
